items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Kenyon Avenue is a location (street/address) mentioned in the context of where the interviewee lived as a boy, not a person.

ctx.x: There was a big record and music shop up town in Cincinnati on 6th Street by the name of [Chubb] Cub & Steinberg who had sponsored the orchestra that was playing at Castle Farm. This fellow told us that his name was Saughtercamp and that he was considered the best dance pianist in Cincinnati and some other towns in Ohio, but he had never heard a pianist who could play as much as Edgar Hayes. He gave Edgar a rendez-vous to meet him a few days later because he wanted Edgar to get on the list of piano players that…

Edgar started making piano rolls but I never heard any that he made. Another thing that Saughtercamp told Hayes the night that he sat at our dining room table was that Edgar had forgotten more piano than he (Saughtercamp) would ever be able to play. That was a great compliment for Edgar Hayes coming from a man who was considered the best white dance band pianist in our part of the country.
